text:
oncall-bot: PAGER: high-severity - GPU pool us-west-2-a reporting sustained queue growth and runtime errors. Trigger: queue_length > 200% for 10m; Xid/CUDA errors rising. Paging @channel.

Maya (SRE): I'm seeing the same in metrics. Queue growth started ~10:02 UTC. autoscaler not bringing new nodes, stuck at 48 active GPUs. Error rate (kernel/Xid) jumped ~18% in last 5m.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): I'm on it. Re-running autoscaler diagnostics now. Can someone post the autoscaler logs?

Devon (Platform): grabbing logs. Looks like scale decisions are being dropped due to quota check failing: 
```
ERROR: scale_request rejected: requested_nodes 8 would exceed project_quota 48
context: project=redwood-client-prod region=us-west-2
```
We hit the hard quota.

Maya (SRE): That matches the alert — scale limit reached. Also see a lot of OOMs on gpu-driver pods and `Xid` 86/89 kernels on some nodes. Likely effective capacity is lower than nominal.

Lee (Runtime Eng): Confirming: driver logs show repeated process OOMs and GPU reset cycles. Sample: 
```
[2024-05-12T10:05:12Z] nvidia: GPU 2: Tainted - Xid 86
[2024-05-12T10:05:19Z] runtime: process crashed: out-of-memory
```
We suspect a memory leak in the driver/kernel interaction after a recent kernel patch. Rolling back kernel hotpatch might recover effective capacity.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Evict non-critical batch jobs from the GPU pool to reduce queue. 2) Request temporary quota bump from cloud (Devon), 3) Fall back high-latency requests to CPU-safe endpoints (Maya). Can we do the evictions now?

Devon (Platform): Eviction script queued. Running `kubectl` drain on low-priority node pool: 
```
kubectl get pods -n gpu-serving -l priority=low -o wide
kubectl drain node/gpu-node-14 --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets --force
```
Started at 10:12 UTC.

Priya (Customer Success): Heads-up — two customers (alpha-bot and data-analytics-saas) flagged latency/500 errors since ~10:06 UTC. Alpha-bot is in us-west region. I'm drafting a brief to send to their CSMs. Any ETA on mitigation?

Maya (SRE): Evictions are reducing queue by ~12% so far. But driver resets continue on ~4 nodes, each reset dropping 1 GPU from capacity. Effective capacity down ~22%. If resets continue we won't recover unless we patch or reboot nodes.

Lee (Runtime Eng): Patch rollback option: roll back 2024-05-10 kernel hotpatch on affected node image. That requires instance self-reboot and ~7 minutes per node. We should prioritize nodes with highest reset counts. I'm preparing a selective rollback playbook.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): Agree. Do a canary rollback on node/gpu-node-07 which has the highest Xid count. Coordinate with SRE for load shifting.

Lee (Runtime Eng): Canary rollback kicked off at 10:20 UTC for gpu-node-07. Logs: 
```
initiating kernel rollback -> snapshot restore -> reboot
node/gpu-node-07: rebooting
```

Maya (SRE): Shifting low-priority traffic off node-07. Observability shows node comes back at 10:27 UTC and GPU resets drop on that host. Queue length dips ~9% after that node returns.

Devon (Platform): Quota bump request submitted to cloud support at 10:22 UTC (ticket #CS-3912). If approved we'll add 8 GPUs to the pool. ETA from cloud support ~30-45m per initial message.

Priya (Customer Success): Sharing a quick customer note: "We are investigating elevated latency for some requests in us-west and are applying remediations; we'll update as we have an ETA." Sent at 10:25 UTC to affected accounts.

Maya (SRE): After canary rollback, observed behavior: Xid errors on node-07 stopped, but two other nodes still showing resets. We'll roll the rollback on next-high nodes one-by-one. Need to coordinate so autoscaler doesn't think nodes are unhealthy and double-add.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): Sequence: (1) keep evicting low-priority pods until queue < 1.2x baseline, (2) sequential rollback/reboot of 2 more nodes (gpu-node-12, gpu-node-19), (3) if cloud quota bump arrives, add capacity. Anyone object?

Lee (Runtime Eng): No objections. I'll prepare a short script to mark nodes temporarily unschedulable to prevent autoscaler race: 
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-12
kubectl annotate node/gpu-node-12 rollback_in_progress=true
```
Then reboot, uncordon after checks.

Maya (SRE): Eviction progress: queue reduction steady but slow. Current queue_length = 2.4k (was 6.1k at peak). Throttling still in effect for some routes. Error rate is trending down but customer-impacting routes still above SLO.

Devon (Platform): Cloud support replied: temporary quota bump approved +8 GPUs for 2 hours. We'll start provisioning once we have at least two nodes fully healthy. Ticket #CS-3912 updated at 10:39 UTC.

Priya (Customer Success): Customers acknowledged the note. Alpha-bot CS reported partial throughput recovery for some endpoints at 10:37 UTC. Good signal.

Maya (SRE): Status update 10:45 UTC: node-12 rollback in progress; node-19 scheduled next. Effective capacity improved to ~85% after node-12 came back. Queue now 1.1k. Still throttling at the edge for heavy streaming routes.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): Provisioning the +8 GPUs now. Spinning up nodes with the pre-patched image to avoid reintroducing regression. Starting at 10:47 UTC.

Lee (Runtime Eng): Important note: we saw one node show kernel panic during reboot attempt — held by platform team, investigating. For safety, I'm pausing further reboots until we confirm the panic cause.

Devon (Platform): Panic trace attached to ticket: "oops: gpu driver state machine encountered invalid pointer during init" — looks like a corner-case when driver re-inits after heavy OOMs. We'll coordinate with runtime to ensure safe driver restart sequence.

Maya (SRE): Interim mitigations summary (applied):
- evicted low-priority workloads (started 10:12 UTC)
- canary rollback on node-07 (10:20-10:27 UTC)
- node-12 rollback completed (10:45 UTC)
- requested and approved +8 GPU quota (10:39 UTC)
- started provisioning additional healthy nodes (10:47 UTC)

Priya (Customer Success): Sending second customer update at 10:50 UTC with improved ETA: "We've applied mitigations and are seeing partial recovery. We expect most throughput to be restored within 30-45 minutes pending node provisioning. We'll follow up as nodes come up."

Jordan (Infra Oncall): New nodes are joining the cluster. Health checks passing for first 2; GPUs ready. Autoscaler has not been able to scale because of quota, but platform provisioning bypassed it. Adding them to routing at 10:55 UTC.

Maya (SRE): By 11:00 UTC, queue down to 420, error rates near baseline, latencies trending back within SLO for most customers. Affected customers reported better performance.

Lee (Runtime Eng): Postmortem action items (immediate):
- rollback hotpatch to stable kernel across pool images (short-term)
- add preflight stress test for driver re-init sequence (mid-term)
- add escalation path to block autoscaler from interpreting rolling reboots as scale-down (short-term)
- improve metrics for 'effective_gpu_capacity' that subtracts GPUs in reset state (short-term)

Maya (SRE): Paging summary for the incident (to be copied into incident doc):
- Impact: queue growth, elevated latency and errors for some us-west customers; two customers reported issues.
- Root cause: kernel/driver interaction regression after recent hotpatch causing GPU resets (Xid/OOM) and effectively reducing available GPUs. Autoscaler attempts blocked by project quota at scale limit, delaying recovery.
- Mitigations: evicted low-priority jobs, sequential kernel rollback and reboots, requested quota bump and provisioned healthy nodes, customer communications.
- Recovery time: significant recovery at ~11:00 UTC; full verification ongoing.

Priya (Customer Success): I'll coordinate follow-ups and impacted-customer RCA notes once engineering finalizes root cause and timeline.

Jordan (Infra Oncall): I'll start drafting the incident timeline and coordinate on the postmortem doc. Oncall handing off to Maya for incident wrap and follow-up.

Maya (SRE): Acknowledged handoff. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If anything flares, re-pager. Closing thread when cleanup is done. :white_check_mark:
